identity.title: [Codex goals] Allow replacing a blocked goal when work is redirected

values.task_boundary: Classify code authority and produce a truthful reviewed routing result; implement only if an actual repository-owned goal replacement seam exists.
deliverables: Six typed C-SDLC cards with explicit planning and validation estimates
Exact external authority and upstream next-action contract
Independent readiness review with all findings resolved
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Repository evidence distinguishes ADL policy and telemetry consumers from the implementation that admits or rejects create_goal
AC-2: The routing result names the OpenAI Codex goal-tool service as external mutation authority unless a concrete repo-owned seam is found
AC-3: The historical blocked goal remains blocked with its status and accounting preserved
AC-4: The exact upstream contract covers explicit replacement or supersession, history retention, accounting retention, and fail-closed active-goal overwrite
AC-5: No ADL code, policy workaround, local goal store, or implementation PR is introduced without repository code authority
AC-6: Design, diagram, six typed cards, deterministic validation, and independent readiness review are current and truthful
dependencies: Codex platform create_goal, get_goal, and update_goal contracts
An upstream Codex product owner able to change thread-goal admission and persistence
repo_inputs: Repository-wide source search for create_goal, update_goal, get_goal, and the exact failure message
non_goals: Implementing a second goal database in ADL
Undocumented reverse engineering of Codex internals
